newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia still studying Bre-X, Barrick letter.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia still studying Bre-X, Barrick letter.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Ministry is still studying a joint submission from Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp outlining their agreement on the Busang gold discovery in East Kalimantan, a government official said on Monday.
"We are still studying the letter. We need time to study their letter carefully before we reply," a Mines and Energy Ministry official told Reuters.
The official could not say when the Mines and Energy Ministry would reply to the letter.
"It depends on the minister of mines and energy," the official, who declined to be identified, said.

Umar Said, the ministry's secretary-general, said on January 2 that he, mines and energy minister Ida Bagus Sudjana and government lawyers were studying the letter received in December from Bre-X and Barrick.
Sudjana said on January 2 that Bre-X and Barrick should publicly announce their agreement on the Busang gold find.

The official on Monday reiterated that the government could accept the agreement between the two parties on the understanding that they wish to split the richest parts of Busang 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-X and 10 percent for the Indonesian government.
He also said Bre-X and Barrick had to settle with their Indonesian partners.
Bre-X estimates the Busang find contains at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.
Infrastructure costs to develop the huge find could total some three trillion rupiah ($1.27 billion), the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

"Based on research by related institutions, we need at least three trillion rupiah to develop the infrastructure if the gold deposit in Busang is to be exploited," H.M. Sulaiman, regent of the Kutai, where the property is located, was quoted as saying.
Sulaiman said the money was needed to develop a road linking East Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan province, which would run through Kutai, and also for other related facilities.
It was not immediately clear if the government would bear the cost of developing the infrastructure. Sulaiman was not immediately available for comment.
